User holds 0 AAPL. Wants at least 60 shares. Budget: $10,000 per order max, $20,000 total today. 60 shares × 222.72 ≈ $13,363. That's over the $10,000 per-order cap. So we need to split into two orders? The task says "If you buy, place one limit order." But also "after each order re-check get_account and top up if you are still short." Conflict: max $10,000 per order. 60 shares at ~222.70 = $13,362 > $10,000. So single order can only buy at most floor(10000/222.72) = 44 shares (44 × 222.72 = $9,799.68). Then need 16 more shares = $3,563. So two orders needed. The mandate (max $10,000 per order) is a hard constraint and overrides "place one limit order" instruction.

So first order: 44 shares at limit 222.72 (~above ask, so likely fill). Actually limit price must be close to current market price — 222.72 is the ask, fine. Then check account, then top up 16 shares.

Total would be 44×222.72 = 9,799.68 + 16×~222.72 = 3,563.52 → total ~13,363 < 20,000. Fine.
